description: The Originals: The beginning of human history, the coders of the future. We are a six developer syndicate blending our ancient roots with cutting edge web development and data science. From the cradle of humanity to the vanguard of innovation, we are here to transform raw space data into the solutions that will sustain tomorrow.
summary:
Field Shift is an interactive web platform built to help smallholder farmers and agricultural planners make sense of complex satellite data. In Ethiopia, shifting climate patterns and unpredictable rainfall constantly threaten crop yields. The problem isn't a lack of data, but rather that existing environmental data is too fragmented or technical for everyday farmers to use. We developed Field Shift to bridge this gap.

Our application pulls live climate telemetry directly from the NASA POWER Agroclimatology API and Esri Earth Observation layers. It transforms raw numbers—like 7-day cumulative rainfall, surface temperature, and vegetation health (NDVI)—into a simple, visual dashboard. To make this data actionable, we built a Multi-Season Crop Rotation Planner tailored for Ethiopian staple crops, helping farmers naturally restore soil nitrogen. We also integrated Fshift AI, a smart agronomy engine that reads the live NASA data to give specific advice, like switching from water-heavy maize to drought-resistant sorghum during dry spells. 

By removing the need for complex GIS software, Field Shift empowers local communities to build resilient, data-driven food systems.
details:
What does it do or how does it work? Field Shift is an interactive agricultural platform that translates live satellite data into actionable insights. It fetches climate telemetry from the NASA POWER API and Esri Earth Observation layers, transforming raw metrics into an intuitive dashboard featuring an interactive map, real-time environmental indicators, and a Crop Rotation Planner. An integrated AI agronomy engine (Fshift AI) analyzes this data alongside visual leaf scans to provide localized farming advice.

What benefits does it have? Field Shift removes technical barriers to Earth observation data, requiring no specialized GIS software. It delivers immediate field vitals and translates them into practical steps. The Crop Rotation Planner helps manage soil health across 12 Ethiopian staple crops, while Fshift AI provides real-time guidance on mitigating drought risks, such as adopting resilient crop alternatives during dry spells.

What is the intended impact of the project? By democratizing access to critical environmental data, Field Shift empowers smallholder farmers and agricultural planners in Ethiopia to make proactive, climate-resilient decisions. Our goal is to prevent soil exhaustion, mitigate drought vulnerability, and improve regional food security.

What tools, coding languages, hardware, or software did you use?

  • Frontend: HTML, CSS, JavaScript, Tailwind CSS.
  • Mapping: Leaflet.js, OpenStreetMap (Nominatim), Esri World Imagery.
  • Data & AI: NASA POWER Agroclimatology API, Google Gemini API (via secure localStorage).
  • Version Control & Hosting: GitHub, Netlify.

    "" Judge Testing Instructions (Fshift AI) To evaluate the live Fshift AI agronomy engine on our Smart Analysis page, please use the following temporary Google Gemini API key when prompted by the interface:AQ.Ab8RN6IoT09e_bACBfZUE7I4wgfF9uj-N7nrYSDS8_cIz399kA(Note: This key is securely restricted and provisioned exclusively for NASA Space Apps evaluation).""

How is your project creative? Field Shift creatively unites geospatial mapping, live API telemetry, and Generative AI into a single workflow. Instead of just displaying raw charts, the platform actively interprets NASA evapotranspiration data to drive our Crop Rotation Planner and Fshift AI, turning abstract climate anomalies into specific, localized agronomic actions.

What factors did your team consider? We prioritized user accessibility, designing a zero-friction interface for non-technical users. For local relevance, we tailored our planner specifically to 12 Ethiopian staple crops. Scientifically, we ensured data transparency by engineering a 3-day temporal lookback window to account for satellite processing latency, complemented by clear methodology documentation.
